title: हिलेपानी गाउँमा वाम्बुले पितृकार्य खाउमा  {Babbule Patriarchal Ritual Khauma at Hilepani Village}
nepali: ‘खाउमा’ किरात वाम्बुले राई समुदायले सम्पन्न गर्ने विभिन्न रीतिथितिहरूमध्ये एक मुख्य पितृकार्य तथा संस्कार हो । यो पितृकार्य परिवारका कुनै सदस्यको मृत्यु भएको वर्ष ‘बर्खान्त’को रूपमा ‘कुयामो खाउमा’ (अशुभ पितृकार्य) भनेर र घर–परिवारमा सुख–शान्ति छाओस् भनेर वा विवाह कर्म वा नयाँ घर निर्माण कार्य सम्पन्न भएको वर्ष वा घरपरिवारमा सुख–शान्ति छाओस् भनेर दुई-चार वर्षको अन्तरालमा ‘फूरी खाउमा ‘(शुभ पितृकार्य) भनेर सम्पन्न गर्ने गरिन्छ । यो पितृकार्य मानव सभ्यता र सृष्टिको मिथकसँग जोडिएको परापूर्वकालदेखि मानिँदै आइएको एक पुरानो संस्कृति हो । यो सम्पन्न गर्न ठ्याक्कै तीन दिन समय लाग्दछ, जुन निकै खर्चिलो पनि छ । खाउमा वाम्बुले राई जातिको परिचय दिने एक मौलिक संस्कृति हाे । तर धर्म तथा संस्कृति परिवर्तन हुँदै जाने कारण यस्ताे संस्कृति लाेप हुने पनि सम्भावना छ । अलिखित मुन्धुम विधिमा आधारित यस संस्कारको अध्ययन ओखलढुङ्गा जिल्लाको हिलेपानी गाउँमा गरिएकाे हाे । याे संस्कृति हाल लोपोन्मुख अवस्थामा पुगेकाे छ । मुख्य मुन्धुमी कुलगुरु (नाक्सो) नहुनु, कतिपय सामग्री प्राकृतिक रूपमै नपाइनु, चौतारो बनाउन र सुम्दी–सिली नाच्नलाई समेत अर्को गाउँको संस्कृतिकर्मी ल्याउनु पर्ने परिस्थिति आउनु जस्ता कारणले हिलेपानी गाउँमा खाउमा लगायत अन्य परम्परागत् मुन्धुमी संस्कार–संस्कृतिहरू लोप हुने खतरामा रहेको सङ्केत गर्दछ ।
american_english: 'Khauma' is a major ancestral rite and sacrament among the various customs and traditions performed by the Kirat Wambule Rai community. This ancestral rite is performed in the year a family member passes away as an annual death observance ('Barkhanta') under the name 'Kuyamo Khauma' (inauspicious ancestral rite), and, so that peace and happiness may prevail in the household or in the year a marriage ceremony or new house construction is completed or so that peace and happiness may prevail in the family, it is performed at intervals of two to four years under the name 'Phuri Khauma' (auspicious ancestral rite). This ancestral rite is an ancient cultural tradition observed since antiquity, linked with the myth of human civilization and creation. Performing this takes exactly three days, which is also quite expensive. Khauma is an authentic cultural tradition that defines the identity of the Wambule Rai people. However, owing to changing religion and culture, there is also the likelihood of such culture disappearing. The study of this sacrament, based on the unwritten Mundhum ritual system, was conducted in Hilepani village of Okhaldhunga district. This culture has currently reached an endangered state. Factors such as the absence of a chief Mundhum lineage priest (Nakso), the natural unavailability of certain materials, and the circumstance of having to bring in cultural practitioners even from another village to build resting platforms (chautaro) and dance the Sumdi-Sili indicate that in Hilepani village, Khauma along with other traditional Mundhum rites and cultures faces the risk of extinction.
british_english: 'Khauma' is a principal ancestral rite and ceremony among the various customs and rituals performed by the Kirat Wambule Rai community. This ancestral ritual is performed in the year a family member passes away as the annual death rite ('Barkhanta') designated as 'Kuyamo Khauma' (inauspicious ancestral rite), and, to ensure peace and happiness prevail in the home and family or in the year a wedding or new house construction is completed or so that peace and harmony prevail in the household, it is carried out at intervals of two to four years designated as 'Phuri Khauma' (auspicious ancestral rite). This ancestral ceremony is an ancient cultural practice observed since time immemorial, linked with the mythology of human civilisation and creation. Completing this takes precisely three days, which is also rather costly. Khauma is an indigenous cultural tradition that provides the distinctive identity of the Wambule Rai people. Yet, owing to continual shifts in religion and culture, there is also the possibility of such traditions dying out. The study of this ritual, founded on the unwritten Mundhum liturgy, was conducted in Hilepani village of Okhaldhunga district. This cultural heritage has now reached an endangered state. Factors such as the absence of the principal Mundhum spiritual preceptor (Nakso), the natural unavailability of certain items, and having to bring in cultural practitioners from another village even to erect resting platforms (chautaro) and perform the Sumdi-Sili dance signify that in Hilepani village, Khauma alongside other traditional Mundhum rites and ceremonies is in danger of disappearing.
